**Droid finished @magnus919's task** —— [View job](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/actions/runs/37151251688)

---
![Security Review](https://img.shields.io/badge/security%20review-ran-blue)

The HTTP advisory path does not apply the operator-configured sensitive-engine policy, allowing public disclosure of sources the policy designates sensitive. The remaining reviewed changes did not yield other high-confidence actionable findings.
@droid Please review the current candidate, including sensitive-policy rejection compatibility, read-boundary cache derivation, and canonical result-count gating for the Jev advisories.

**Droid finished @magnus919's task** —— [View job](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/actions/runs/37151275336)

---
The advisory logic mostly follows the intended read-boundary and sensitive-source constraints. One scope mismatch can disclose unavailable sources that the media-constrained search would not dispatch.

Runner code review of candidate `f4ab41d486f77725304aa1b58dac9c03fb5ae0f3`:

- Traced HTTP and MCP read boundaries: advisories are attached after SearchService reads/executes; they are not added to canonical caches or snapshots. MCP captures the canonical total before `max_results` slices it; a regression verifies six canonical results still advise when one is shown.
- Inspected policy handling: the shared sensitive policy rejection remains unchanged and metadata-free. Advisory source names are excluded using catalog sensitivity and context/policy sensitive sets. Large-result reranking notes are suppressed for sensitive scopes. The repaired policy slice passes 53 tests, including zero-dispatch mixed-list rejection.
- Checked scope relevance and configured controls: explicit engines/categories/media, configured topic routing and general fallback use declared capability metadata; no inferred classifier or extra dispatch/model calls. Configured providers suppress their unavailable notes. Cached MCP responses update public credential notes from current configuration without re-dispatch.
- Verified output safety and evidence claims: messages exclude query text and credentials; HTML escapes them and uses collapsed disclosure; max three notes. Jev benefits are attributed to operator-reported production experience and per-query gain remains unmeasured. The advice does not assert full-result reranking support or any current candidate limit.
- Offline baseline/final matrix: 14/14 eligible notes and 8/8 quiet controls; adapter counts and stable non-advisory payloads match. This validates the disclosure contract, not agent task success or ranking uplift.

No remaining code finding from this review. Normal full-suite CI and all other applicable checks still gate merge; this review alone does not authorize bypassing them. Droid review is still running and will be inspected when available.

Both substantive Droid findings are fixed: HTTP passes the startup-frozen operator sensitive policy into advisory derivation, and media eligibility intersects all source scopes. Added real HTTP policy and category/explicit media regression tests. Existing metadata-free sensitive rejections remain intact. Please re-review the new candidate.

@droid Please review current SHA 876da1be842b716040cf91a0b5b865cb842b7fe6 after both earlier findings were fixed. Check the HTTP operator sensitive policy, media intersection, and unchanged fail-closed errors.

**Droid finished @magnus919's task** —— [View job](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/actions/runs/37151709398)

---
No high-confidence actionable issues remain in the reviewed candidate. Both prior findings about media-scope filtering and operator-configured sensitive-source disclosure are addressed in the latest diff; the existing metadata-free fail-closed sensitive policy rejection is preserved.

Final candidate review: `6c590affdee8a9ecfb203be413547136e48cabc1`.

Droid's substantive follow-up reports no remaining actionable findings and verifies the HTTP operator-sensitive policy, media intersection and metadata-free fail-closed rejection fixes. The only subsequent delta from `876da1b` is the HTTP regression fixture: remove full application lifespan startup, inject current runtime objects directly, close the client, and restore globals via monkeypatch. I reviewed that complete delta and the current helper/HTTP/MCP/formatter paths. The affected advisory/integration/policy sequence passes 69 tests, with no live dispatch. The broader corrected contract slice passed 253 tests, and the frozen matrix remains 14/14 eligible and 8/8 quiet controls with identical non-advisory payloads and adapter calls.

Both initial Droid findings are fixed; my earlier review missed them, and that earlier review must not be treated as independent proof of those boundaries. New tests cover each. No remaining finding on the current candidate. Full-suite CI must pass on this exact SHA before merge. Local full reruns stalled during MCP transport setup and were interrupted; retain those logs instead of treating them as passing results.
